hypothesis: Electric organs (Darwin's stated example) occur in fish lineages that are separated on an independently estimated phylogeny by lineages lacking electric organs, so that the organ must have arisen more than once rather than being inherited from one common ancestor; the same holds for light-producing organs in insects (his second example).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered: on the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree induced on a fixed list of electric-organ-bearing fish families and a fixed list of non-electric fish families, count (i) the Dollo minimum number of independent origins = number of maximal clades whose tips are all electric, and (ii) the Fitch parsimony minimum number of state changes. SUPPORTS if, for the electric-fish case, (i) >= 3 and (ii) >= 3 (no reconstruction with a single origin and fewer than three changes exists). The insect light-organ case is scored the same way and reported; it does not decide the verdict because the claim is existential ('has sometimes').
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: REFUTES if the electric-organ-bearing families form a single clade in the synthetic tree (Dollo origins = 1, Fitch changes = 1). MIXED if Dollo origins = 2, or if the two statistics disagree about whether >= 3 changes are needed. If the Open Tree API is unreachable or fewer than 80% of the listed families map to the tree, the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable).
interpretation: Darwin's claim has two parts: that similar organs sometimes arose independently in distantly related organisms (testable from a phylogeny) and that natural selection acting on analogous variations produced them (a mechanism not tested here). Only the first, pattern part is tested. 'Electric organs of fishes' = the families with electrogenic organs in the modern literature: Torpedinidae, Narcinidae, Narkidae, Hypnidae (Torpediniformes), Rajidae (skates), Mormyridae and Gymnarchidae (Mormyroidea), Gymnotidae, Apteronotidae, Sternopygidae, Hypopomidae, Rhamphichthyidae (Gymnotiformes), Malapteruridae (electric catfish) and Uranoscopidae (stargazers); Darwin knew Torpedo, Gymnotus and the electric catfish. 'Luminous organs of insects' = Lampyridae, Phengodidae, Rhagophthalmidae, Elateridae (Pyrophorini), Keroplatidae (Arachnocampa, Orfelia). 'Independently estimated phylogeny' = the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree, whose fish and insect backbones derive mostly from molecular studies. Independence is counted on a tree whose tips are families; origins within a family are not counted separately, which makes the count conservative.
